releases.name: Sailing now
releases.blurb: What is in the build you are playing.

items.title: San Francisco Bay, replayed
items.text: Real wind, gusts, tide and tidal stream from NOAA for 14 July 2024, with real depths, coastline and the bridges.

items.title: Three boats
items.text: A 30 ft sloop, a 38 and a 45 ft performance cruiser, each with her own polar, heel and handling. Name her and choose her colours.

items.title: Hands on the boat
items.text: Steer, trim and tack by pointing at the wheel, boom and winches. No sailing buttons on the screen.

items.title: Autopilot and crew
items.text: Hold a heading, a wind angle or the route while the crew trims. It beats to windward and tacks for the mark.

items.title: Chartplotter and passage plan
items.text: Waypoints, leg times from the forecast, plan against actual, and a forecast you can scrub through.

items.title: Sailing in company, first cut
items.text: Open the same link as a friend and see each other's boats live, on one clock, and hail each other.

items.title: First lesson and coaching hints
items.text: An optional guided first sail, then quiet hints when a sail has been luffing for a while or the boat is stuck in irons.

items.title: Point of sail on the instruments
items.text: The readout names what she is doing: close-hauled, beam reach, running, in irons, and which tack.

items.title: Places to sail to
items.text: McCovey Cove, Ayala Cove, Sam's in Tiburon and more are on the chart. Click one to head there.

items.title: Skipper's logbook
items.text: Miles, hours, marks and knockdowns, added up across every sail and shown beside the rest of the fleet.

items.title: Crash gybes
items.text: Let the boom come across on its own in a breeze and she rounds up, or goes flat on her side.

items.title: Gust warnings
items.text: The readout shows a gust on its way and how long until it arrives. A strong one raises an alert and drops time back to real speed.

items.title: Release notes
items.text: What's new lists every update, and a marker tells you when there is one you have not read.

items.title: Racing, first cut
items.text: Call a race or join one: a course, a countdown, pace boats on the autopilot, live places and a finish time.

items.title: Wind tunnel view
items.text: The air over your sails drawn as smoke lines, and the wind angle your trim is asking for. Scott's idea.

items.title: Who is on the water
items.text: A list of every boat sailing with you, what she is doing, and her range and bearing.

items.title: Anchoring, moorings and a night aboard
items.text: Stop the boat on her anchor, a mooring buoy or a dock, with sails stowed, and sleep through to the morning.

items.title: Crab pots and fishing
items.text: Drop pots and come back for them, troll or bottom fish for the Bay's real species, and log what you land.

items.title: Ashore by kayak
items.text: Launch the kayak from the anchored boat, paddle in on the tide, land at the Bay's bars and beaches, and paddle home.

items.title: San Juan Islands, first cut
items.text: A second water to choose on the way in, baked from NOAA's wind and Salish Sea tide model for a real summer day.

items.title: bajaregatta.com
items.text: The game on its own website, with other boats, hails and races, no Claude account needed.

items.title: A common start
items.text: Everyone who enters a race is towed to a berth in the start area.

items.title: Race marks and a guide line
items.text: Buoys at every mark, a beacon on the next one, and a line on the water to steer by.

items.title: Wildlife on the Bay
items.text: Porpoise, sea lions, seals, pelicans, cormorants, gulls and the odd humpback, where and when they really are.

items.title: The real skyline
items.text: The towers, piers, Alcatraz and both bridges a Bay sailor steers by, lit at dusk.

items.title: One-design racing
items.text: Everyone in a race sails the same boat, chosen by whoever calls it.

items.title: Spinnaker, reefing and knockdowns
items.text: An asymmetric spinnaker for off the wind, a reef for when it blows, and a boat that goes over if you carry too much.

items.title: Experience points and ranks
items.text: Points for good seamanship and for racing, and nine ranks to climb.

releases.name: Release 1 · The Bay together
releases.blurb: The first target. Many people on the same Bay at once, racing or just out for a sail.

items.title: Accounts and profiles
items.text: Sign up with an email. Your skipper profile, boats, fit-out and logbook live with your account, on any device. The logbook in this build is the first piece.

items.title: Race days
items.text: Start lines with a penalty for being over early, mark rounding rules, fleets by boat class, a season table, and results that every boat agrees on.

items.title: A shared Bay to roam
items.text: Drop in any time and see who else is out and where they are on the chart. No race needed: just go sailing together.

items.title: Meet up somewhere
items.text: Pick a place and tell the others: McCovey Cove for the ball game, Ayala Cove on Angel Island, the dock at Sam's in Tiburon.

items.title: Somewhere to go ashore
items.text: A bar-hop card that stamps each place you land, stepping straight ashore at a dock, then drawn docks and beaches and other crews you can see in their kayaks.

items.title: Talk to the fleet
items.text: Text hails are in. Next: voice on a VHF channel, so it sounds like the real thing.

items.title: Accounts on the website
items.text: Shared water and races already work on bajaregatta.com. Next: sign-in by email for everyone, so logbooks, votes and feedback follow you.

items.title: A catch worth cooking
items.text: Pots and lines shown on the chart, tides and seasons that matter, and a catch the galley can turn into supper and morale.

items.title: Come aboard
items.text: Paddle over to a friend's boat, go aboard for a drink, and hand over a fish you caught.

items.title: Collisions that count
items.text: Hit another boat and both are damaged: slowed, holed or dismasted by how hard. A bad one ends your race until you ask for a tow back to the start.

releases.name: Release 2 · Passages
releases.blurb: Long races and deliveries that run for days, like a flight simulator for the sea.

items.title: The Baja Ha-Ha
items.text: San Diego to Cabo San Lucas with two stops: a rally start, then days at sea in real time.

items.title: Watches and crew
items.text: Set a watch schedule. Crew have skill and fatigue, and a tired watch misses a wind shift.

items.title: Provisions and tanks
items.text: Load water, food and fuel before you go. Run short and it costs you.

items.title: Call me when she needs me
items.text: Leave her on autopilot and get a text or an email when the wind shifts, a reef is due or land is near.

items.title: Night in port
items.text: Marinas on a passage: a berth for the night, fuel, water and stores, and the harbour office in the morning.

items.title: Out the Gate to the Farallones
items.text: Fifty-two miles of ocean swell, the bar and fog, as the first step offshore.

items.title: Feeding the crew
items.text: What you catch and what you stowed decide what is for dinner, and a fed crew stands a better watch.

items.title: Round the Horn
items.text: The Roaring Forties: down the 40th parallel and round Cape Horn. Days at sea, big wind and sea, watches, sail changes and weather routing.

releases.name: Release 3 · Charter waters
releases.blurb: Warm water, short hops and a catamaran.

items.title: San Juan Islands, finished
items.text: The first cut is sailable. Still to come: races that go with the tide, ferries, trees and towns on the islands, and the fish that live there.

items.title: The 42 ft catamaran
items.text: No heel to warn you: reef by the numbers. Two engines for docking.

items.title: British Virgin Islands
items.text: Trade winds, short hops and a mooring ball every night: Tortola, Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke and Anegada.

items.title: Greece
items.text: The Cyclades and the meltemi, stern-to in a harbour for dinner.

items.title: Croatia
items.text: The Dalmatian coast: Split, Hvar, Vis and Korcula, with the afternoon maestral and the bora to watch for.

items.title: Points that show
items.text: Your rank beside your name on the water, a season table, and a sound when you make a new rank.

items.title: Prize money
items.text: Win races, earn a purse.

items.title: Upgrade the boat
items.text: New sails, a spinnaker, a folding prop, better instruments: each one changes how she sails.

releases.name: Always · Seamanship and the real world
releases.blurb: Making the sailing truer, release after release.

items.title: Sail any day in the archive
items.text: Pick a date, right up to yesterday, and get that day's real wind and tide from NOAA's records. Never live feeds.

items.title: Jib alone or main alone
items.text: Roll the jib away or drop the main right down and sail under either sail.

items.title: A better coach
items.text: Hints that notice more: pinching, sailing by the lee, a missed layline, a foul tide you could have dodged.

items.title: Laylines and tide gates on the chart
items.text: See when to tack and when the stream turns in your favour.

items.title: Night and fog
items.text: Navigation lights, lit buoys, the city at night, and San Francisco's fog.

items.title: Wildlife everywhere you sail
items.text: Orcas and eagles in the San Juans, turtles and frigate birds in the islands, and animals close enough to see well without being told.

items.title: Phones and tablets
items.text: Touch already steers and trims by dragging the boat's parts. Everything that is on a key today needs a way in without a keyboard.

items.title: Controls that explain themselves
items.text: Make it plain what can be grabbed and what each key does, without reading a list first.

items.title: More of the shore
items.text: Cliffs on Alcatraz, the low-rise city, Sausalito and Tiburon, pier numbers and the Marina breakwater.

items.title: A dinghy to mash around in
items.text: A fast little tender with an outboard, beside the kayak.

items.title: The boat's radio
items.text: Yacht rock and eighties stations to put on while you sail or lie at anchor.

items.title: Snorkel and spearfish
items.text: Over the side at anchor: an underwater view, kelp and reef, and a speargun for supper.

items.title: More boats
items.text: Something small and quick: a dinghy or a sportboat to throw around.

items.title: Life at anchor
items.text: A swim off the stern, the grill on the rail, sundowners, a hammock on the foredeck.

items.title: The engine
items.text: Motor in and out of harbour and through a calm, with a fuel gauge and a battery to keep an eye on.

items.title: Fishing from the kayak
items.text: A hand line or a short rod from the kayak, where the fish and the tide decide how it goes.

releases.name: Expedition · Voyages from history
releases.blurb: A second way to play, chosen at the start: historical voyages you try to survive, navigating the way they did.

items.title: Shackleton's boat journey, 1916
items.text: Six men, a 22 ft lifeboat, 800 miles of the Southern Ocean from Elephant Island to South Georgia. Faithful and harsh: gales, ice on the deck, a tainted water cask, and four sun sights to find an island. First to be built.

items.title: Columbus, 1492
items.text: Palos to the Bahamas on the trade winds, with a crew that wants to turn back. The first of the old ships.

items.title: Da Gama, 1497
items.text: Lisbon to Calicut round the Cape for pepper: the wide swing into the Atlantic, scurvy, and a hostile coast.

items.title: Magellan, 1519
items.text: Sanlucar to the Spice Islands the wrong way round: mutiny, the Strait, ninety-nine days across the Pacific, and eighteen men home.

items.title: Pirates of the Caribbean trade, about 1715
items.text: Trade and chase. A fight is decided by men, ships, guns and seamanship in the wind and sea of the day, not by aiming a cannon.
